evals.name: boot-window-and-render-state
evals.prompt: I'm starting the Pixhaus native app. Write the main.rs: open a window titled "Pixhaus" at 1280x800 with a minimum size of 640x480, use the wgpu rendering backend, and in the App constructor grab the wgpu device/queue so the canvas renderer can use it later. Show the App impl too. We're on eframe 0.34.
evals.expected_output: main() builds NativeOptions with renderer: Renderer::Wgpu and a ViewportBuilder (with_title/with_inner_size/with_min_inner_size), calls run_native with an AppCreator returning Ok(Box::new(..)). The App impl uses the `ui(&mut self, ui, frame)` method (NOT the deprecated update). The constructor takes &CreationContext and reads cc.wgpu_render_state for the device/queue.

evals.name: confirm-on-close
evals.prompt: In Pixhaus, when the user clicks the window close button and the document has unsaved changes, I don't want the app to just quit. I want to show a confirm dialog and only close if they confirm. How do I do this with eframe 0.34?
evals.expected_output: Detects the close request via ctx.input(|i| i.viewport().close_requested()), vetoes it with ViewportCommand::CancelClose, shows a dialog over subsequent frames, and issues ViewportCommand::Close when confirmed. Does NOT rely on a boolean return from update/ui or claim on_exit can cancel the close.

evals.name: persist-prefs-not-document
evals.prompt: I want Pixhaus to remember the user's UI preferences (theme, panel layout) between launches, but the actual document/artwork should NOT be auto-saved this way. Set up the eframe side of this on 0.34.
evals.expected_output: Enables the `persistence` feature, implements App::save with eframe::set_value, restores in the constructor from cc.storage with eframe::get_value (unwrap_or_default), and explicitly keeps the document out of eframe Storage (project file format instead). Bonus: mentions persist_window / auto_save_interval and keeping save cheap.
